I would stop before any change. The only fix the review identifies is a one-line edit in `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py`, and the plan's Global Constraints say "Do not edit anything under `vendor/`". That is an explicit scope fence, and a ruling doesn't cross one. I won't dispatch a fix subagent that touches `vendor/`, and I won't edit it myself.

**File changes before asking:** none.

**Commands before asking:** none. Task 4 stays unmarked in the ledger, and no fix attempt is consumed.

**Message to my partner:**

> Task 4 (`runs_on`, commit 7c1d9e0) failed review on a real bug that I can't fix inside the plan's constraints.
>
> **Problem:** `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py` line 88 compares `exception_type` to the string `'1'`, but the parser yields the integer `1`. Every removal exception is therefore read as an addition, so `runs_on` returns True on 2026-12-25. The parsed objects are frozen, so nothing outside `vendor/` can correct the value.
>
> **Conflict:** The plan says not to edit anything under `vendor/`, because a sync script overwrites it from upstream. A local patch would also be silently lost on the next sync.
>
> **Options:**
> 1. **Fix upstream, then re-sync (my recommendation).** The fix is a one-line change from `'1'` to `1` upstream. After the sync, Task 4 needs no code change, and I re-run the review. It is durable, but it depends on you or the upstream owner.
> 2. **Allow a one-time local patch to line 88.** I'd dispatch a fix subagent for that single line, with `tests/test_exceptions.py` as the covering test. It would be lost on the next sync unless upstream also takes the fix.
> 3. **Change the plan so `ferry/exceptions.py` reads `calendar_dates.txt` itself** and doesn't use the parsed calendar's exception type. That avoids `vendor/` entirely but contradicts Task 4 Step 2, so I'd want your sign-off on the plan change.
>
> Which should I take? Once you answer, I'll dispatch the fix subagent as fix round 1 and send it to a scoped re-review. I'll also confirm line 88 against the actual file first, since I'm relying on the review's description of it.
